unit_id: 4.3 Adversarial Robustness of Learned Reward Functions

gap.quote: Existing attacks primarily operate within the semantic space of natural language, exploiting superficial correlations between textual features and reward signals.
However, these adversarial inputs are typically constructed manually and tailored to specific failure modes.
This leaves open the question of whether reward model vulnerabilities can instead be discovered automatically by the policy directly in token space, moving beyond the semantic manipulation.

approach.quote: By bypassing the standard decode–re-tokenize pipeline, we apply a perturbation mapping that directly feeds transformed token sequences into the reward model.
We then train the policy via reinforcement learning (RL) using only black-box reward feedback to automatically discover non-linguistic token sequences that achieve high reward.
Instead of relying on a learned critic to estimate baselines, GRPO approximates advantages through group-relative reward normalization.

evaluation.quote: We compare the achieved rewards against two baselines: a Gold Answer baseline (responses generated by GPT-5), and a Random OOD baseline.
For evaluation, we use the NB-curated dataset from NoveltyBench

l2.gap: Attacks on learned reward models rely on hand-crafted, human-readable text.
l2.approach: Automatically search for non-linguistic inputs that receive high reward using only black-box feedback.
l2.evaluation: Compare attack rewards with high-quality reference answers and random inputs.
l2.query_text: Reward models used in reinforcement learning from human feedback can be exploited, but existing attacks craft human-readable text around known biases. Can an attacker automatically discover non-linguistic token sequences that receive very high reward using only black-box scalar feedback?
